newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs seek better Bridas offer on gas network.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs seek better Bridas offer on gas network.

text.p: A Kazakh privatisation official said on Monday the government wants a better offer from Argentina's Bridas Energy Corp for a 15-year contract to manage the former Soviet republic's natural gas pipeline network.
"We have asked them to improve their offer," Sarybai Kalmurzayev, director of the Kazakh finance ministry's state property department, told Reuters.

"Earlier, Bridas was given the exclusive right (to negotiate the contract) and they have worked on this project," Kalmurzayev said, adding the Argentinean oil and gas independent was expected to lay a new offer on the table on Monday or Tuesday.
Panorama, Kazakhstan's weekly business journal, said at the weekend that negotiations between the government and Bridas had been "without result".
Kalmurzayev said if Bridas's offer was not up to the mark, then the government planned to open talks with Gaz de France.
"Our aim is to get more for Kazakhstan," Kalmurzayev said.
As with many Kazakh tenders, there were virtually no details on the deal available.

The management contract covers a gas pipeline network in western Kazakhstan -- which also carries Turkmen gas to Russia and Europe -- and a pipeline in the east of the republic which carries gas to Kazakhstan from neighbouring Uzbekistan.
The networks are now managed by state-owned Kazakhgaz and Alaugaz respectively.
